title: Combining feature-based approaches with graph neural networks and symbolic regression for synergistic performance and interpretability
why: Recent (2025-09) MatterVial paper: augments MODNet with pretrained GNN/ROOST latent features on Matbench tasks; the closest recent feature-fusion competitor (pool holds only its Figshare data record).

title: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration
why: Recent (2025) composition-only stacked generalization of diverse domain-knowledge experts (ECSG); the most direct prior for stacking diverse composition experts.

title: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model
why: TabPFN (Nature 2025): the small-tabular foundation model behind the in-pool ICL materials paper; a likely expert and baseline for a CPU-only small-data stack.

title: Benchmarking materials property prediction methods: the Matbench test set and Automatminer reference algorithm
why: Defines the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks, the official folds and the Automatminer baseline the candidate is measured on.

title: Materials property prediction for limited datasets enabled by feature selection and joint learning with MODNet
why: MODNet leads the official leaderboard on matbench_steels and is near the top on expt_gap; the main baseline to beat.

title: Compositionally restricted attention-based network for materials property predictions
why: CrabNet is the standard composition-only attention baseline and a top expt_gap leaderboard entry (Ax/SAASBO CrabNet); also a candidate stack expert.

title: A General-Purpose Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Properties of Inorganic Materials
why: Magpie composition descriptors: the feature backbone the tree and kernel experts in the stack will be built on.
